---
title: "Initial and Final Residuals in Solver Output"
description: "What the Initial residual, Final residual and No Iterations values in the OpenFOAM log mean, verified against the source code."
categories: [OpenFOAM, linear solvers, convergence]
---

Every time an OpenFOAM solver solves a linear system it prints a line like this (the numbers are
illustrative):

```
smoothSolver:  Solving for Ux, Initial residual = 0.0123, Final residual = 9.8e-05, No Iterations 4
GAMG:  Solving for p, Initial residual = 0.0457, Final residual = 0.000412, No Iterations 7
```

This page explains exactly what those numbers are. Everything here was checked against the source
code of both OpenFOAM versions; see [Source code references](#sec-sources). Where the two versions
differ, it says so.

## What is being solved

Each `solve()` call works with a linear system for one field $\psi$ (`p`, `k`, one component of `U`, …):

$$
\mathbf{A}\,\psi = \mathbf{b},
$$ {#eq-system}

where $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are the matrix and source as they stand at the moment of the
solve, including boundary condition contributions and any modifications made beforehand, such as
under-relaxation. The residual vector for a given approximate solution $\psi$ is

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{A}\,\psi .
$$ {#eq-residual-vector}

## How the residual is computed {#sec-definition}

OpenFOAM does not report $\lVert\mathbf{r}\rVert$ directly. It reports a **scaled L1 norm**: the sum of
the absolute residuals over all cells (and all processors), divided by a normalisation factor $n$:

$$
\text{residual} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_i \left| b_i - [\mathbf{A}\psi]_i \right| .
$$ {#eq-scaled-residual}

The normalisation factor is computed once per solve, from the starting field, in
`lduMatrix::solver::normFactor`:

$$
n = \sum_i \Big( \big| [\mathbf{A}\psi]_i - [\mathbf{A}\mathbf{1}]_i\,\bar\psi \big|
             + \big| b_i - [\mathbf{A}\mathbf{1}]_i\,\bar\psi \big| \Big) + \varepsilon ,
$$ {#eq-norm-factor}

where

- $\bar\psi$ is the arithmetic (not volume-weighted) average of $\psi$ over all cells,
- $[\mathbf{A}\mathbf{1}]_i$ is the sum of the coefficients in row $i$ (`sumA`), so $[\mathbf{A}\mathbf{1}]_i\,\bar\psi$ is
  the matrix applied to a uniform field equal to the average,
- $\varepsilon$ is a tiny constant (`solverPerformance::small_`) that prevents division by zero.

In words, $n$ measures how far both $\mathbf{A}\psi$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are from what a uniform field would
give. Because this scaling is relative to the field's own variation, the residual is dimensionless and
does not depend on the field's units or on adding a constant to $\psi$. The source code comments note
that at convergence @eq-norm-factor is equivalent to $2\sum_i |b_i|$.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why the first residual is often exactly 1
If $\psi$ is uniform (as it often is at the first iteration of a case initialised with uniform
values), then $\mathbf{A}\psi = [\mathbf{A}\mathbf{1}]\,\bar\psi$. The first term of @eq-norm-factor
vanishes, $n$ becomes $\sum_i |r_i|$, and @eq-scaled-residual gives exactly 1.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## openfoam.com: the `norm` keyword
openfoam.com lets you choose the normalisation with a `norm` entry in the solver dictionary in
`fvSolution`: `default` and `L1_scaled` both use @eq-norm-factor, and `none` sets $n = 1$, so the
reported value is the raw, unscaled $\sum_i |r_i|$. openfoam.org has no such option and always uses
@eq-norm-factor.
:::

## Initial residual

The **initial residual** is @eq-scaled-residual evaluated with the field *before the linear solver does
any work*, i.e. using the values from the previous outer iteration or time step as the starting guess.
The linear solvers compute it first, then set the final residual equal to it.

It answers the question: *how well does the current solution satisfy the equations as they have just
been assembled?* Because $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are rebuilt from the latest solution at each outer
iteration, the initial residual is the quantity that tracks convergence of the **non-linear, coupled
problem** (the SIMPLE or PIMPLE loop), not just the linear solve. This is why convergence plots
and `residualControl` use initial residuals (see @sec-convergence-controls).

## Final residual

The **final residual** is @eq-scaled-residual evaluated with the field *after the linear solver stops*,
using the same normalisation factor $n$ computed at the start. It only tells you **how accurately this
particular linear system was solved**. It says nothing about whether the overall solution has converged,
since the next outer iteration assembles a new system.

## When the linear solver stops

After each iteration, the solver checks (in `SolverPerformance::checkConvergence`) whether

$$
\text{final residual} < \texttt{tolerance}
\quad\text{or}\quad
\big(\texttt{relTol} > 0 \ \text{and}\ \text{final residual} < \texttt{relTol} \times \text{initial residual}\big),
$$ {#eq-stopping}

and keeps iterating while this is false and fewer than `maxIter` iterations have been done, or while
fewer than `minIter` iterations have been done. `tolerance`, `relTol`, `minIter` and `maxIter` are set per
field in `fvSolution`.

The convergence check is also made *before* the first iteration, using the initial residual. If the
initial residual already satisfies @eq-stopping (and `minIter` is 0), the solver returns without
iterating.

## No Iterations

`No Iterations` is the number of solver iterations performed. What one iteration means depends on the
solver:

- **PCG / PBiCGStab:** one Krylov iteration.
- **GAMG:** one multigrid V-cycle.
- **smoothSolver:** the counter increases by `nSweeps` each time. The residual is only evaluated after
  every `nSweeps` sweeps, so the count is always a multiple of `nSweeps` (default 1).

## Vector and tensor fields

For fields such as `U`, segregated solution is used by default: each component is solved as a separate
scalar system, so you see separate lines for `Ux`, `Uy` and `Uz`, each with its own normalisation
factor, residuals and iteration count. Components that are not solved (for example the empty direction
in a 2D case) are skipped and do not appear. Where a single number is needed for a vector field (for
example in `residualControl`), OpenFOAM uses the largest component residual.

## Reading the log in practice

`No Iterations 0`
: The initial residual already met `tolerance` (or `relTol`). This is common for well-converged
  steady cases or small time steps. It is not an error.

Final residual ≈ `relTol` × initial residual
: The solver stopped on `relTol`. This is intentional for most fields in SIMPLE/PIMPLE, where there
  is no point solving tightly an equation whose coefficients will change next iteration. PIMPLE cases
  usually use `relTol 0` in the `*Final` solver entries, so the last corrector is solved to `tolerance`.

Final residual not much smaller than initial, `No Iterations` = `maxIter`
: The linear solver is failing to converge. Check the solver and preconditioner choice, mesh quality
  and boundary conditions.

Initial residuals falling steadily, then levelling off
: Typical of a converged steady case. Where they level off depends on the mesh, discretisation and
  physics, so there is no universal target value.

Small initial residuals but a wrong answer
: Residuals measure how well the discrete equations are satisfied, not discretisation error or
  whether the setup is physically right. Also monitor physical quantities (forces, flow rates, probe
  values).

## Convergence controls and residual output {#sec-convergence-controls}

The two versions differ in exactly which initial residual they use.

**openfoam.org**

- `SIMPLE { residualControl { p 1e-4; … } }` compares the **initial** residual of the **first**
  solve of each field in the iteration against the given tolerance.
- `PIMPLE { outerCorrectorResidualControl { p { tolerance …; relTol …; } } }` compares the
  **initial** residual of the first solve in the current outer corrector against `tolerance`, and its
  ratio to the initial residual of the first solve in the time step against `relTol`.
- The `residuals` function object writes the **initial** residual of the first solve of each field in
  each time step.

**openfoam.com**

- `SIMPLE { residualControl { … } }` compares the **initial** residual of the **first** solve in the
  iteration against the given tolerance.
- `PIMPLE { residualControl { p { tolerance …; relTol …; } } }` is not checked on the first or the
  final outer corrector. From the second outer corrector on, it compares the **initial** residual of
  the most recent solve against `tolerance`, and against `relTol` times the initial residual recorded
  at the second outer corrector.
- The `solverInfo` function object writes the initial residual, final residual and iteration count of
  the first solve of each field in each time step.

Tools such as `foamLog` and most residual plots show **initial** residuals.

The same normalisation factor is used by all the standard `lduMatrix` solvers: PCG, PBiCG, PBiCGStab,
GAMG and smoothSolver in both versions, plus FPCG and PPCG in openfoam.com. If a future version changes this, update the page and the commit references.
